title: Induced principal-adic topology on submodules over valuation-ring restricted series
statement: Let $K$ be a complete field with a nontrivial real-valued nonarchimedean absolute value, let $V=\{a\in K:|a|\le1\}$ be its valuation ring [def-trf-valuation-ring], and fix $\pi\in V$ with $0<|\pi|<1$. For $r\ge0$ set $S=V\langle T_1,\ldots,T_r\rangle$, the ring of formal series whose coefficients tend to zero [def-trf-restricted-series-presentation]. Let $M$ be a finitely generated $S$-module [def-weil-finitely-generated-module] and $N\subseteq M$ any $S$-submodule. For every integer $m\ge0$ there is an integer $n\ge m$ such that $\pi^n M\cap N\subseteq\pi^m N$. Here $\pi^k L=\{\pi^k x:x\in L\}$ for any $S$-module $L$. Thus the neighbourhoods $\pi^n M\cap N$ induce on $N$ exactly its principal $\pi$-adic topology; $N$ need not be finitely generated, and $M$ need not be torsion-free.

source.place: Section 2.3, Lemma 7(ii), printed pp. 131-132 (PDF pages 132-133), specialized to the restricted-series algebra itself in case (V). Primary PDF read online; local archival copy WANTED.

proof.text: Define $P=\{x\in M:\pi^k x\in N\text{ for some }k\ge0\}$. This is an $S$-submodule containing $N$: if $\pi^a x,\pi^b y\in N$, put $c=\max(a,b)$ to obtain $\pi^c(x+y)\in N$, and $\pi^a(sx)=s\pi^a x\in N$. Negatives and zero follow from the submodule axioms. It is saturated: $\pi^j x\in P$ gives $\pi^{j+k}x\in N$ for some $k$, hence $x\in P$.

source.place: Section 2.3, proof of Lemma 7(ii), printed p. 132 (PDF page 133); explicit saturation and elementwise expansion of the stated containments.

proof.text: Apply [lem-trf-restricted-saturated-submodule-finite] to $P\subseteq M$. Its field, valuation ring, restricted-series algebra and finite-module hypotheses are precisely those of the item, and step 1 verifies saturation. It gives generators $p_1,\ldots,p_t$ for $P$ as an $S$-module.

source.place: Section 2.3, proof of Lemma 7(ii), printed p. 132 (PDF page 133); explicit saturation and elementwise expansion of the stated containments.

proof.text: For each generator choose $c_i\ge0$ with $\pi^{c_i}p_i\in N$, as the definition of $P$ allows. Put $c=\max(\{0\}\cup\{c_1,\ldots,c_t\})$. Then for every $p=\sum_i s_i p_i\in P$, one has $\pi^c p=\sum_i s_i\pi^{c-c_i}(\pi^{c_i}p_i)\in N$. Thus $\pi^c P\subseteq N$, including $P=0$ with its empty generating family and $c=0$.

source.place: Section 2.3, proof of Lemma 7(ii), printed p. 132 (PDF page 133); explicit saturation and elementwise expansion of the stated containments.

proof.text: Given $m\ge0$, take $n=m+c\ge m$. If $x\in\pi^nM\cap N$, write $x=\pi^{m+c}y$ with $y\in M$. Since this power of $y$ lies in $N$, the definition gives $y\in P$, whence $\pi^c y\in N$ by step 3 and $x=\pi^m(\pi^c y)\in\pi^mN$. Conversely $\pi^mN\subseteq\pi^mM\cap N$ because $N$ is a submodule. The two families of zero-neighbourhoods are therefore cofinal and define the same topology. No cancellation of a power of $\pi$ in $M$ has been used.

reviewed.note: mechanical checks by tools/merge_delivery.py; mathematics reviewed in full by NT-cc-Q67-0509dac82 (reviewer sub-agent of L); spot-checked: I read Bosch, Lectures on formal and rigid geometry (preprint heft378), §2.3, from the online PDF: case (V) on p.129, Thm 4 (Raynaud–Gruson) on p.130, Lemma 7(i)/(ii) and its case-(V) proof on pp.131–132. The item is exactly 7(ii) with A=V<T> and the new node lem-trf-restricted-saturated-submodule-finite is exactly 7(i). V is π-adically complete with ideal of definition (π), which puts it in case (V), and Bosch's I^k x⊂N is π^k x∈N. No hypothesis is added or dropped and nothing is weakened. Steps: (1) the saturation P is a saturated submodule (elementary, checked). (2) The new node, applied with identical hypotheses, gives P finitely generated. (3) The maximum of finitely many exponents gives π^cP⊂N; the empty family is handled. (4) n=m+c; y∈P because π^{m+c}y∈N; no cancellation of π, so torsion in M is fine; cofinality in both directions. The new node is statement-only and self-contained, cites def-trf-valuation-ring, def-trf-restricted-series-presentation and def-weil-finitely-generated-module, and records three kinds of search (Mathlib candidates need Noetherian hypotheses). I tested it on P=0, P=M, M=S/(π) and r=0, where the torsion-free quotient is free; the non-saturated maximal ideal of V is excluded. It is not a clause of the item. An rg -L search of the DAG found no duplicate: 053E lem-trf-valuation-finite-type-module-presentation covers algebras of finite type, and the parent lem-trf-restricted-quotient-complete would make a cycle. Both nodes are in unit sk-i-curve-zero, with no tool_uses.
